rationale: Baseline completed only 40/320 optimizer steps, with first-update first-step KL 0.18107 dominated by mean shifts.

Head scale 0.1 reduced initial mean absolute magnitude from 0.40306 to 0.04014, completed 319/320 steps, and had the lowest validation height error 0.03972m and lower yaw error. Its net force 112.12N is worse, so it is not accepted as physically successful.

LR 3e-5 completed 296/320 steps and improved height and net force to 0.06739m and 44.59N. LR 1e-5 gave similar height 0.06569m and force 42.49N; select the interior 3e-5 level to combine with already-reduced head sensitivity rather than minimizing KL or selecting a search boundary.

Head scale 0.01 had worse height 0.07762m despite a lower initial KL; std 0.4 worsened height/force; std 0.1 failed old-log-prob verification before the first optimizer step and is excluded with its original failure preserved.
The LR-plus-head combination is a falsifiable hypothesis to improve the pose/contact tradeoff, not an observed combination result or a single-factor causal claim.

No numerical or physical success threshold was pre-established. All completed evaluations have finite metrics and zero resets but nontrivial pose/contact error; relative signals justify bounded confirmation, not long training or deployment.
